skill.name: agent-browser
skill.description: Controls a remote Playwright browser through inference.sh for navigation, snapshots, form actions, screenshots, video, proxy routing, uploads, and JavaScript execution.
skill.summary: Automate browser sessions with compact element refs, screenshots, recordings, and page actions.
skill.author: inference-sh-skills

security_audit.summary: Most static command, URL, path, and device findings are documentation or shell-template false positives. Confirmed risks include browser capture upload, SOCKS proxy support, cookie extraction guidance, sensitive session recording examples, and arbitrary page JavaScript execution. No prompt injection attempt was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: Screenshots and recordings can expose sensitive page content.
remediation.suggestion: Default recording to off, require explicit approval for authenticated pages, and add redaction guidance for screenshots and videos.

remediation.issue: Authentication documentation includes cookie extraction and printing.
remediation.suggestion: Remove cookie extraction examples or restrict them to authorized debugging with warnings never to log session cookies.

remediation.issue: Proxy documentation frames rotation as rate-limit avoidance.
remediation.suggestion: Replace rate-limit avoidance examples with compliant geo-testing guidance and explicit respect for site policies.

remediation.issue: Custom JavaScript execution can access sensitive page data.
remediation.suggestion: Document safe usage boundaries and warn users not to run extraction scripts on pages without authorization.

remediation.issue: Shell templates interpolate URLs and paths into command inputs.
remediation.suggestion: Validate input URLs, quote session variables consistently, and document safe output directory handling.

1. **Open** - Navigate to URL, get `@e` refs for elements
| `open` | Navigate to URL, configure browser (viewport, proxy, video recording) |
| `snapshot` | Re-fetch page state with `@e` refs after DOM changes |
| `interact` | Perform actions using `@e` refs (click, fill, drag, upload, etc.) |
| `screenshot` | Take page screenshot (viewport or full page) |
| `execute` | Run JavaScript code on the page |
| `close` | Close session, returns video if recording was enabled |

content.user_title: Automate Browser Sessions with Agentic Refs
content.value_statement: AI agents often need reliable browser control without parsing full page DOMs. This skill provides compact refs, actions, screenshots, and reusable workflows.
actual_capabilities: Open remote browser sessions with URL, viewport, proxy, and recording options.
Return compact @e element refs for clicks, fills, selections, uploads, and drag actions.
Refresh page snapshots after navigation, form submission, or dynamic content changes.
Capture viewport or full page screenshots and optional WebM session recordings.
Run JavaScript in the active page to extract text, links, counts, or selected content.
Provide shell templates for form automation, authenticated sessions, and content capture.
limitations: Requires the inference.sh CLI and an authenticated account before use.
Browser content, screenshots, and recordings may be handled by the remote service.
Element refs change after navigation and must be refreshed before later actions.
The skill does not enforce site terms, scraping policy, or sensitive data safeguards.

use_cases.title: Validate Web Flows
use_cases.description: Run repeatable browser steps, capture evidence, and inspect failures in staging or production-like pages.

use_cases.title: Collect Web Research
use_cases.description: Open pages, extract visible text and links, and save screenshots for later analysis.

use_cases.title: Prepare Support Documentation
use_cases.description: Record browser workflows with cursor indicators and capture screenshots for customer-facing guides.

prompt_templates.title: Open and Inspect a Page
prompt_templates.prompt: Open the target page with agent-browser, list the visible interactive elements, and summarize the page purpose.

prompt_templates.title: Fill a Known Form
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the current snapshot refs to fill the contact form fields, submit it, and verify the resulting page state.

prompt_templates.title: Capture Evidence for a Bug
prompt_templates.prompt: Start a recorded browser session, reproduce the issue step by step, take a full page screenshot, and close the session.

prompt_templates.title: Extract Structured Page Content
prompt_templates.prompt: Navigate to each approved URL, refresh refs after every page change, extract visible text and links, and note any access failures.

output_examples.input: Inspect a product page and identify the main actions.
output_examples.output: The page loaded successfully. The main actions are search, add to cart, size selection, and account sign in.

output_examples.input: Record a failing checkout path for debugging.
output_examples.output: The workflow produced a screenshot, a short recording, and a note that the payment step failed after address entry.

output_examples.input: Extract links from an approved documentation page.
output: Captured the page title and visible navigation links.
Saved a full page screenshot for reference.
Reported stale refs after navigation and refreshed the snapshot.

best_practices: Use only approved URLs and respect site terms, rate limits, and access controls.
Refresh snapshots after navigation, submissions, modals, or any dynamic page update.
Disable recording and redact screenshots when pages may contain credentials or private data.
anti_patterns: Do not use stale @e refs after a page changes or reloads.
Do not record login, payment, admin, or customer data workflows without explicit approval.
Do not use proxy rotation to bypass rate limits, identity controls, or geographic restrictions.

faq.question: What does this skill control?
faq.answer: It controls an inference.sh browser session that uses Playwright-style actions and compact element refs.

faq.question: Does it require another tool?
faq.answer: Yes. The documentation requires the inference.sh CLI and login before browser automation works.

faq.question: Can it handle authenticated sites?
faq.answer: Yes, but authenticated pages can expose sensitive data through snapshots, screenshots, recordings, and cookie examples.

faq.question: Can it upload files?
faq.answer: Yes. It can submit local file paths to file input elements during browser interactions.

faq.question: When should I take a new snapshot?
faq.answer: Take a new snapshot after navigation, form submission, scrolling that reveals content, or dynamic page updates.

faq.question: Is proxy support available?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill documents HTTP, HTTPS, and SOCKS proxy settings, which require careful governance.
